sections.h2: What makes Hamilton County different for a home seller?
sections.html:
Hamilton County is the urban end of this group of East Tennessee counties. It follows the Tennessee River around Chattanooga, borders Georgia to the south and touches ten other counties. The legislature created it on October 25, 1819, and in 2020 it ranked as the fourth most populous county in the state. Lookout Mountain, Ruby Falls and Point Park sit within it, and Interstates 24 and 75 cross it.

Chattanooga is the seat. Other municipalities are Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy-Daisy, Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain and Walden. Each one matters on a tax bill, because the answer to who collects, and at what rate, changes by address.

The Census Bureau reports for Hamilton County:

  • 390,833 residents in July 2025, up 6.5 percent from April 2020
  • 176,983 housing units, with 63.9 percent owner-occupied
  • $312,800 as the median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024
  • $76,183 median household income, and 37.5 percent of adults 25 and older holding a bachelor's degree
  • 1,887 building permits in 2025

That median value runs well above the $207,500 shown for Greene County and $210,900 for Hamblen County, so the same percentage mistake costs more here.

sections.h2: Who bills and who collects property tax in Hamilton County?
sections.html:
The Assessor of Property values the land and buildings, the Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and the Trustee collects. The Trustee's office is in Room 210 of the Hamilton County Courthouse on Georgia Avenue in Chattanooga. A second counter is at 6125 Preservation Drive, Suite 101, in the Bonny Oaks Industrial Park. Both are open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and the number is (423) 209-7270.

The Trustee also collects the city taxes for Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy Daisy and Walden. Chattanooga runs its own. Its City Treasurer is at City Hall, 101 E 11th Street, Room 100, with the phone at (423) 643-7262 and email ptax@chattanooga.gov. A Chattanooga owner therefore pays two separate bills.

The Assessor of Property, Marty Haynes, is at 6135 Heritage Park Drive and answers at (423) 209-7300. The Assessor's FAQ is clear that the office only values property and has no say over rates, so a bill can climb with no change in value if a rate goes up.

sections.h2: What is the Hamilton County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The county's certified rate announced on June 3, 2025 was $1.51 per $100 of assessed value, down from $2.23. The county mayor's release called it the lowest since 1941 and tied it to the four-year reappraisal. The new rate went onto the bills mailed in fall 2025. The Assessor said about two thirds of owners would pay the same or less in county tax than in 2024.

Chattanooga's own page lists a city rate of 1.93 per $100 of assessed value. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value and commercial property at 40 percent. A Chattanooga house appraised at $312,800, the county median, has an assessed value of $78,200, and the bill is that figure divided by 100 and multiplied by the county and city rates. For this year's county rate, check with the Trustee, since the county's certified rate is reset after each reappraisal and the commission may adjust it each budget year.

sections.h2: When are Hamilton County taxes due and what happens if I pay late?
sections.html:
Bills go out near the end of September. Payment opens October 1 and runs through the last day of February. Today is November 15, 2026, so the bill is open with no interest yet. Interest of 1.5 percent a month, which the county puts at 18 percent a year, starts on March 1.

The Trustee lists the following payment rules:

  • Partial payments are accepted
  • A mailed payment counts as late if the post office does not postmark it by the due date, and office meter dates are not accepted
  • Online payments count on the date of the transaction
  • A current bill with the original notice can also be paid at any First Horizon Bank branch in Hamilton County

Tennessee does not require the county to mail a notice, and the county says failing to receive one does not cancel interest. Chattanooga adds 1 percent interest and a half percent penalty monthly after February, and files unpaid prior-year taxes with Hamilton County Chancery Court in March. Unpaid taxes can lead to a tax sale each June, with a one-year redemption period.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hamilton County assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with an informal review by the Assessor's staff. Look up your parcel on the Assessor's property search and sales comparison tools, or call 423-209-7990 to talk with an appraiser. The Assessor asks that informal reviews be requested before May 20.

If that does not settle it, ask the Assessor's office for a county Board of Equalization appeal form. The board sits during June, and filings are taken through the first week of June, so call for the exact cutoff. After that the State Board of Equalization is available, with an August 1 or 45-day limit, and a hearing before an administrative judge. Whoever appeals must prove the value, and the best proof, says the state, is comparable sales with adjustments.

Hamilton County reappraises every four years. The last round took effect in 2025 and the next is set for 2029. Between those years a value usually stays put, so an appeal in a non-reappraisal year centers on errors such as wrong square footage or condition.

sections.h2: What tax relief exists in Hamilton County?
sections.html:
The state reimburses part of the tax for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled veterans. The county's FAQ shows a 2025 income cap of $37,530, and the state brochure sets the 2026 figure at $38,470 of 2025 income, with a $33,600 value cap for elderly and disabled owners and $175,000 for veterans. Hamilton County says it matches the state relief. Appointments are made at the Bonny Oaks office at (423) 209-7799.

The tax freeze for homeowners 65 and older works differently here. Hamilton County itself is not on the Comptroller's list of 28 freeze counties, but the City of Chattanooga adopted a freeze in 2017 with a 2026 income limit of $63,470. That freeze applies to the city bill only. Greenbelt, a separate break for farm or forest land of 15 acres or more, is handled by the Assessor.

sections.h2: What happens to Hamilton County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Bills go to the owner of record. The Trustee tells new owners to check the closing statement or ask the title company who owes what, because payment depends on the date of transfer, and unpaid tax stays attached to the property. Before you list, pull the balance from the Trustee's online property tax inquiry to see current and prior years for both the county and, if it applies, Chattanooga.

A seller who inherited the house or fell behind can arrange to have the balance paid from sale proceeds at the table. The Register of Deeds, at (423) 209-6560, records the deed and collects the state transfer tax.

faqs.q: What is the Hamilton County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The certified county rate set in 2025 was $1.51 per $100 of assessed value, down from $2.23. Chattanooga lists its own city rate of 1.93 per $100. Call the Trustee at (423) 209-7270 to confirm what applies to your bill.

faqs.q: When are Hamilton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They can be paid from October 1 through the last day of February. Interest of 1.5 percent a month begins March 1. Notices are mailed near the end of September but are not legally required.

faqs.q: How often does Hamilton County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Every four years. The Assessor's FAQ says the last reappraisal was 2025 and the next is 2029. Between reappraisals an owner can still ask for review if the property record has an error.

faqs.q: Do I pay both Chattanooga and Hamilton County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. A Chattanooga property owner receives a county bill and a separate city bill. The county Trustee collects only for seven smaller cities, while Chattanooga's City Treasurer collects its own tax at City Hall.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Hamilton County?
faqs.a: Yes. The state relief program reimburses owners 65 or older whose income is within the limit, and the county says it matches the state amount. Chattanooga also has a tax freeze for seniors. Call (423) 209-7799 to set a time.
